# Roadmap Prioritization

Read live issue and project state: Status, Priority, Target release, labels,
parent/child links, and blocking relationships. The tracker is authoritative
for current state; roadmap documents explain rationale only.

Prefer, in order: production or security incidents; structural fixes that
prevent recurrence; planning blockers; committed release blockers; failing
tests; maintenance; then new features. Within a tier, prefer work that
unblocks other items.

Parallelize only when there is no dependency and no file or module overlap.
Report readiness, priority, ordering, tracker/document mismatches, and the
evidence inspected. Do not change scope or project fields without explicit
authorization.
